Blueprints

Source: vignettes/blueprints.Rmd
blueprints.Rmd

A blueprint is one section of a spigot app, packaged so that it can be written, read and moved on its own. It holds the section’s pages and whatever they need: the endpoints they call, their templates and partials, and the scripts and stylesheets they load. spigot_app() mounts it under a prefix, and the blueprint itself never says where that is.

Use one when an app has sections that are more than a page each, such as a cars section with a table and a model form, or an admin area, so that app.R lists sections rather than every page and endpoint. A one-page app does not need one. The Templates, static files and blueprints vignette shows the folder layout around them. This one covers what a blueprint is and how its parts are found.

library(spigot)

A blueprint and where it lands

Here is a small blueprint with two pages and one endpoint. The templates are inline text to keep the example short. A real one usually names template files.

page <- function(body) {
  spigot_page(paste0("<html><head></head><body>", body, "</body></html>"))
}

greet <- spigot_blueprint(
  pages = list(
    "/"      = page("<h1>Hello</h1> <a href='greet/about'>About</a>"),
    "/about" = page("<p>A section of the app.</p>")
  ),
  api = spigot_api() |> plumber::pr_get("/hello", function(name = "you") {
    list(message = paste("Hello,", name))
  })
)
greet
#> <spigot_blueprint>
#>   pages:     /, /about
#>   api:       router

Its paths are written as if it were the whole app: its main page is /. The app chooses the prefix when it mounts it:

app <- spigot_app(
  pages = page("<a href='greet'>Greetings</a>"),
  api = spigot_api(),
  blueprints = list("/greet" = greet)
)

Each part of a blueprint mounted at /greet lands here:

Part In the blueprint Served at From one of its pages
A page / /greet <a href="greet">
A page /about /greet/about <a href="greet/about">
An endpoint /hello /api/greet/hello spigot.get("greet/hello")
A static file hello.js in static /greet/static/hello.js <script src="{{static}}/hello.js">

Links on a spigot page are relative to the app’s root, whatever the page’s depth, because spigot gives nested pages a <base href> that points there. That is why the links above start with greet/ and not /greet/: the same page works when the app itself is served under a path, as it is on Shiny Server or Posit Connect. A page that should not depend on the blueprint’s own prefix can use {{static}} for its files (see below). Its links and API calls still name the prefix.

The prefix can have more than one segment, such as "/tools/greet". It cannot be /, and it cannot be under the API’s prefix.

Pages

A blueprint’s pages are the same as spigot_app()’s: one page, served at the prefix, or a list of pages named by path. Every page must be a spigot_page(), because a Shiny UI can only be the app’s own / page. Data, data functions, caching and partials work as on the app’s pages.

When the app is built, spigot checks a blueprint’s pages along with the app’s own. A path that both the app and a blueprint serve is an error that names both:

spigot_app(
  pages = list("/" = page("home"), "/greet/about" = page("mine")),
  api = spigot_api(),
  blueprints = list("/greet" = greet)
)
#> Error:
#> ! The page "/greet/about" of the blueprint "/greet" is also a page of the app.

So is a blueprint mounted under the API:

spigot_app(pages = page("home"), api = spigot_api(), blueprints = list("/api/greet" = greet))
#> Error:
#> ! The blueprint "/api/greet" is under the API prefix "/api", so it would never be served.

The API

A blueprint’s api is a plumber file or a plumber router. spigot mounts it on the app’s router at the blueprint’s prefix, so with the default prefix = "/api" the blueprint’s /hello is /api/greet/hello. It is part of the app’s API, so the app’s checks apply: unless require_session = FALSE, it answers only requests from the app’s own pages, and its endpoints can call spigot_session(), spigot_emit() and the rest. A page calls it like any other endpoint, with the path below the API prefix:

const reply = await spigot.get("greet/hello", { name: "Ada" });

A file is read when spigot_app() builds the app, relative to the app’s root, and its endpoints are evaluated in the environment where spigot_blueprint() was called. For a blueprint defined in the app’s R/ folder, that is the environment Shiny loads R/ into, so the endpoints can use any function defined there:

# R/cars.R
fit_cars <- function(x) {
  fit <- stats::lm(stats::reformulate(x, "mpg"), data = datasets::mtcars)
  list(r_squared = summary(fit)$r.squared)
}

cars <- spigot_blueprint(
  pages = list("/" = spigot_page("list.html"), "/model" = spigot_page("model.html")),
  api = "api/cars.R"
)
# api/cars.R
#* @get /fit
function(x = "wt") fit_cars(x)

A blueprint can leave api out. Its pages can still call the app’s own endpoints.

Templates and partials

A blueprint’s templates are folders searched before the app’s when one of its pages names a template file. For a page of the cars blueprint, spigot_page("list.html") is found in the first of these places that has it:

  1. The blueprint’s templates, in order, such as templates/cars/list.html.
  2. The app’s templates, in order, such as templates/list.html.
  3. The app’s root, list.html.

A blueprint can therefore use the app’s shared templates, or keep its own file under a name the app also uses. Its file wins, and only for its own pages.

Partials follow the same rule, closest first. A page’s own partials win over its blueprint’s, and those win over the app’s. If the app’s partials folder holds nav.html and the blueprint’s holds a nav.html too, {{> nav}} is the blueprint’s nav on its pages and the app’s everywhere else:

cars <- spigot_blueprint(
  pages = list("/" = spigot_page("list.html")),
  templates = "templates/cars",
  partials = "templates/cars/partials"   # its own nav.html
)

spigot_app(
  pages = list("/" = spigot_page("index.html")),
  api = "api.R",
  blueprints = list("/cars" = cars),
  templates = "templates",
  partials = "templates/partials"         # the app's nav.html, head.html, footer.html
)

All of these files are read, and every partial a page uses is checked, when spigot_app() builds the app. A missing file or partial stops the app before it serves anything.

Static files and {{static}}

A blueprint’s static is one folder, served at <prefix>/static. httpuv sends these files directly, without running R, however the app is launched.

Every page of a blueprint with static gets the folder’s URL in its data as {{static}}: cars/static for a blueprint mounted at /cars, relative to the app’s root like every other link. A template can load its files without knowing the prefix:

<link rel="stylesheet" href="{{static}}/cars.css">
<script src="{{static}}/cars.js"></script>

If a page’s data has its own static, that one is used. A page whose data is a function gets static added to what the function returns.

Defining blueprints in R/

Define each blueprint in a file in the app’s R/ folder, one file per blueprint:

myapp/
├── app.R           # spigot_app(blueprints = list("/cars" = cars, "/model" = model))
├── R/
│   ├── cars.R      # cars <- spigot_blueprint(...)
│   └── model.R     # model <- spigot_blueprint(...)
├── api/
│   └── cars.R
├── templates/
│   ├── cars/
│   └── model/
└── static/
    ├── cars/
    └── model/

Shiny loads every file in R/, in alphabetical order, before it runs app.R, so the blueprints exist when spigot_app() asks for them. A blueprint’s paths, like the app’s, are relative to the app’s root, which is the app’s folder when the folder is run. This only happens when the folder is run, with shiny::runApp("myapp"), RStudio’s Run App button, Shiny Server or Posit Connect. See Where paths start.

The site example (run_example("site")) is laid out this way, with a cars blueprint and a model blueprint.

Blueprints are values

spigot_blueprint() returns an ordinary R object, and mounting it does not change it. The same blueprint can be mounted at more than one prefix. Its pages and endpoints are then served under each prefix, and each mount’s pages get their own {{static}}:

app <- spigot_app(
  pages = page("home"),
  api = spigot_api(),
  blueprints = list("/greet" = greet, "/hello" = greet)
)

Copies with different settings come from a function that returns a blueprint. Here, two sections show different columns of the same data:

table_section <- function(title, columns) {
  spigot_blueprint(spigot_page(
    "<html><head></head><body><h1>{{title}}</h1>{{#rows}}<p>{{row}}</p>{{/rows}}</body></html>",
    data = list(
      title = title,
      rows = lapply(do.call(paste, unname(datasets::mtcars[columns])),
                    function(row) list(row = row))
    ),
    cache = TRUE
  ))
}

app <- spigot_app(
  pages = page("home"),
  api = spigot_api(),
  blueprints = list(
    "/engine" = table_section("Engine", c("cyl", "disp", "hp")),
    "/weight" = table_section("Weight", c("wt", "qsec"))
  )
)

Blueprints do not nest: a blueprint has pages but no blueprints of its own. A section deep in a site takes a longer prefix, such as "/tools/greet".

Compared with Flask

Flask spigot
bp = Blueprint("cars", __name__, template_folder=..., static_folder=...) cars <- spigot_blueprint(pages, api, templates, static = ...)
app.register_blueprint(bp, url_prefix="/cars") spigot_app(blueprints = list("/cars" = cars))
@bp.route("/model") "/model" = spigot_page(...) in pages
a JSON route on the blueprint an endpoint in its api, served at /api/cars/...
url_for("cars.static", filename="cars.js") {{static}}/cars.js
blueprint templates searched after the app’s blueprint templates searched before the app’s

The last row is a deliberate difference. In Flask an app’s template overrides a blueprint’s with the same name. In spigot the blueprint’s own file wins, the way its partials do, so a section is not changed by a file another part of the app happens to add.
